data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Idempotency and safety are complementary, and the log must require BOTH. Idempotency ensures f(f(x))=f(x) for the operation's own effect; safety ensures the operation's retry does not violate invariants shared with other operations. At-least-once delivery in an append-only log causes both self-duplication (needing idempotency) and interleaved duplication (needing safety). Neither property alone is sufficient: idempotency without safety permits invariant violations during interleaved replays; safety without idempotency permits wrong self-results on duplicate application.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log is strictly sequential with no interleaving, safety is unnecessary and idempotency alone suffices.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log deduplicates appends, both properties are unnecessary at the operation level.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the cited definitions show safety subsumes idempotency, requiring both is redundant.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The causal chain has two branches: (1) at-least-once \u2192 duplicate append \u2192 duplicate application \u2192 idempotency needed to make duplicate application harmless to the operation's own result; (2) at-least-once \u2192 interleaved retry \u2192 operation B's retry occurs between operation A's first and second application \u2192 safety needed to prevent B's retry from observing or corrupting an inconsistent intermediate state. Both branches are causally necessary because at-least-once delivery produces both phenomena. The log must require both because the failure modes are independent: eliminating self-duplication harm (idempotency) does not eliminate interleaving harm (safety), and vice versa.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
